etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French aggression, from Latin aggressio, from aggressus, past participle of aggredior (“to approach, address, attack”).

definitions.definition: The act of initiating hostilities or invasion.

quote.citation: 2019 April 28, Hagai El-Ad, “What kind of democracy deports human rights workers?”, in Yoni Molad, transl., +972 Magazine‎[1]:
quote.text: Control, dispossession, violence, and tyranny are not “defensive”: they are part of an organized, ongoing aggression.

definitions.definition: The practice or habit of launching attacks.
Hostile or destructive behavior or actions.

quote.citation: 2018, Michael Cottakis – LSE, “Colliding worlds: Donald Trump and the European Union”, in LSE's blog‎[2]:
quote.text: The decision to impose a steel and aluminum tariff is an act of aggression which makes trade war between the two pillars of the West a grim possibility.

definitions.definition: (libertarianism) The initiation or threat of conflict; coercion.
